explanation: or a dog or cat collar with a bell on it.

discriminators: Small, bright and heavily damped: a collar, sheep or sleigh bell is tiny, so its pitch and spectral_centroid_hz are high and its decay_time_seconds_60db is far SHORTER than any other bell here — the strap and the animal's body damp the ring.

It is worn on something moving, so it usually arrives as a repeated jingle (a rhythmic onset train) rather than a single deliberate strike. That combination — bright, short-ringing, repeated — separates it from BELLS-HANDBELL, which is bigger, darker and rung on purpose.
BELLS-LARGE is the opposite extreme: low, and ringing for many seconds.
Orchestral sleigh bells or a kit cowbell are MUSICAL-PERCUSSION / MUSICAL-SHAKEN.

discriminators: The classic ding-dong is two struck chime bars, so expect transient_count near 2 with a clean ring under and after them — a distinctive count for a bell.
Tuned bars are less inharmonic than a cast bell, so inharmonicity sits below BELLS-LARGE and BELLS-HANDBELL, and the ring is shorter than a tower bell but much longer than a tiny BELLS-ANIMAL.
A rasping door BUZZER is not a bell at all — that is ALARMS-BUZZER: sustained, distorted, no decay. The presence or absence of a decaying tail decides it outright.
UCS keeps electronic doorbell chimes here too, which is what caps this at narrowable: a synthesized ding-dong has the envelope but not the inharmonic partials.

explanation: A large flat circular disc hit with a mallet. With v8.2 of the list most of these would now go into MUSICAL-BELLS instead.

discriminators: The longest and most inharmonic ring in the whole taxonomy: a struck disc whose partials are so dense and so detuned that it barely reads as pitched at all — very high inharmonicity with LOW harmonicity, decaying over many seconds.

A gong blooms. Energy migrates upward after the strike through nonlinear coupling, so spectral_centroid_slope_hz_per_second is positive; a cast bell (BELLS-LARGE) rings out with a flat or falling centroid. That bloom, plus the low harmonicity, is the real gong/bell boundary.
Struck with a soft mallet, so the attack is slower than a metal clapper strike.
UCS v8.2 redirects most musical gongs, tam-tams and singing bowls to MUSICAL-BELLS, so this is a shrinking category and text should be trusted over signal when the two disagree.

explanation: dinner bells. Musical bells like HANDBELLS and CARILLION now go into MUSICAL-BELLS.

discriminators: The middle of the bell size ladder, and size is the only real axis: brighter and shorter-ringing than BELLS-LARGE, darker and longer-ringing than the tiny BELLS-ANIMAL. Rung by hand, so several clapper strikes usually appear in one file.

Strong metallic inharmonicity is what makes any of these a bell and not a mallet instrument — MUSICAL-PERCUSSION TUNED bars (glockenspiel, marimba, vibraphone) are tuned to near-INTEGER harmonic ratios, so their inharmonicity is low. High inharmonicity plus a long ring is the archetypal bell.
Handbell choirs and carillons were moved to MUSICAL-BELLS in v8.2; this is the dinner, school and service bell.

explanation: Large bells like a church bell or tower bell

discriminators: Mass sets the pitch. A church or tower bell is LOW (hum well under ~300 Hz), rings for many seconds, and carries the famous inharmonic partial set — roughly 2.0, 2.4, 3.0 and 4.2 times the hum, nowhere near integers. High inharmonicity plus a very long decay_time_seconds_60db plus a low f0 is one of the strongest single signatures in UCS.
Every other bell is smaller, hence higher and shorter: BELLS-HANDBELL and especially BELLS-ANIMAL sit far up in pitch with a fraction of the ring time.
BELLS-GONG rings just as long but is a disc, not a cast bell: much less pitched (low harmonicity) and its brightness RISES after the strike instead of decaying flat.
Peals and tolling give a slow periodic onset train; a single toll is equally valid.
